description: Defaults for custom exercises created from the Build tray. A MODELLED DEFAULT derived from the 247 library exercises (median / most common value per movement_pattern x equipment cell), not evidence. Keys, enums and units are those of exercises.json. Built by tools/build_custom_defaults.py from tools/custom_exercise.py; spec in data/custom-exercise-defaults.md.

fields: muscles (one main mover + optional helpers / minors)
stretch_focused (toggle, default from pattern x main muscle)

toggles.stretch_focused: Hardest when the muscle is stretched

band_ratios.why: Each ratio is the median (and most common value) of library ratings inside its band: main 1.0, helper 0.5, minor 0.3. Minor uses 0.3, not 0.25: 0.3 is the library median for minor, and 0.25 sits exactly on the counting threshold (min_rating_to_count). data/custom-rules.json v1 (the copy-a-template flow) uses minor 0.25; the band form uses 0.3.

library_distribution.note: All non-zero muscles[] ratings of the 247 library exercises, bucketed by the body_map level bands. trace (< 0.25) is not counted by the planner, so the form has no trace band.

id.slug: name lowercased, ASCII-folded, runs of other characters -> "-", trimmed, max 40 chars
id.collision: library ids never start with "custom-" (tested); redraw the 6 random characters until the id is unused among custom exercises; never reuse an id after delete (history keys on it)

errors: name required, 1-60 chars, unique among custom exercises (case-insensitive)
muscles: known ids, each listed once, band in main / helper / minor
warnings: name equals a library exercise name
more than 6 muscles (library median 3 counted muscles)

short_name_rule:
1) name if it fits (<= 16) and is free: kept as typed (a brand stays whole). 2) Otherwise equipment brands (BRANDS) are dropped as a whole
unit, then the name is shortened: drop a parenthetical, library abbreviations (whole words) in order, drop leading words keeping the last two
(the movement noun, e.g. 'Chest Press'), then leading hyphen parts, then the first word shortened with a period ('Concentrat. Curl'), then the last word alone, then a hard cut for one over-long word. 3) If that collides with a library or custom short name and the name had a
brand, use the brand abbreviation as a pinned prefix ('HmS Iso Row') and shorten the rest to fit. 4) Still taken: ' 2', ' 3', ... (dropping
leading words before cutting). A brand fragment can never show: brands are removed or replaced whole before any word is dropped or cut.

short_name.brand_rule: Equipment brands are one unit, matched whole-word and case-insensitive (a space or hyphen between brand words matches either). When the name must be shortened, the whole brand is dropped; only if the result collides with a library or custom short name is the brand abbreviation used as a pinned prefix. A brand is never split, so a fragment like "Strength Iso Row" cannot appear. A name that already fits (<= 16) is kept as typed, brand included.
short_name.abbreviation_rule: whole words, applied in order until the name fits (the library short_name_note abbreviations)

fields.rule: make_id: slug = name lowercased, ASCII, non-alphanumerics -> "-", max 40; redraw on collision. Library ids never start with custom- (tested). Same format as data/custom-rules.json id_format.
trimmed, single spaces, 1-60 chars, unique among custom exercises (case-insensitive)

short_name(): name if it fits (<= 16) and is free; else drop equipment brands as a whole (short_name.brands), drop a parenthetical, library abbreviations, drop leading words keeping the last two, then hyphen parts / a period-marked first word / the last word; on a collision use the brand abbreviation as a prefix; unique with " 2", " 3". Never a brand fragment.
lower median of the cell on primary < accessory < isolation; isolation pattern -> isolation; compound pattern never isolation; core / other never primary
one of the exercises.json equipment values
most common list in the cell, else the equipment, else the rules.json equipment_items token
all 19 muscles; main 1.0, helper 0.5, minor 0.3, others 0. Stimulus per set: a set credits each muscle sets x rating (ratings >= 0.25 count)

head = muscle rating x the pattern's median head/muscle ratio, scaled so the strongest head equals the muscle rating (group = max of heads, as data/custom-rules.json); single-head muscles copy the muscle
"" / [] / {setup: "", cues: [], mistake: ""}; the user may add text
lower median of the cell (always a library value: 0.8, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.5); sets the recovery tier (heavy_axial_compound >= 1.5, other_compound >= 1.1, lighter_compound >= 1.0, isolation)
most common slot list for that movement pattern and main muscle, else the pattern; checked so movement.py movement_pattern(e) == the chosen pattern
one of rules.json movement_patterns.order

ordinals: lower median of the cell (stability from the equipment side); stretch_emphasis 3 when stretch_focused else <= 2; muscle_isolation: compound 1, isolation 2 (3 on stable equipment). flags: the cell majority among unilateral, constant_tension, grip_demand, spinal_load, static_hold, overhead_finish, peak_contraction_focus; the form toggle overrides unilateral; bias flags (upper_chest_bias, ...) are never defaulted
most common list (calisthenics for most bodyweight / rings cells); omitted when empty
only when most of the cell has a fraction: lower median, basis "modeling"; bodyweight_ref and bodyweight_assisted are never set
custom exercises always credit a tracked muscle
true / true (custom: excluded from library suggestion pools, as suggest.py / rank.py / patterns.py already do; estimated: the est. badge)
legacy rules.json patterns key (push / pull ratio, redundant pattern, same-pattern swaps); swap.py already reads e.pattern; the Builder must also register the id in rules.patterns[pattern]

when stretch_focused: the main muscle (if it has a rules.stretch_biased list) plus glutes when glutes are main or helper on a squat / lunge / hinge (the glute stretch rule); register the id in those lists (credit for the per-muscle stretch check)
{low, high, unit, not_to_failure}: the cell's most common whiteboard rep range (unit reps / seconds / meters); register as a per-id rep_ranges override
which cell / fallback each group came from (for the "estimated" tooltip and debugging)

lookup.cells: cells["<movement_pattern>|<equipment>"]: every one of the 10 x 15 combinations, already resolved. source.movement_fields = cell (>= 3 library exercises) | pattern | global; source.equipment_fields = cell | equipment | equipment_rule.
lookup.median: lower median (the lower middle value for an even count), so every default is a value the library actually uses

register: Add the record to the exercise table (EX) used by the planner, analysis, ranker, whiteboard, warm-up and logger.
rules.patterns[record.pattern].push(id) (legacy pattern map: push / pull ratio, redundant pattern, same-pattern swaps).
For m in record.stretch_biased_for: rules.stretch_biased[m].push(id) (per-muscle stretch check credit and stretch share).
rules.rep_ranges.overrides.push({id, exercises: [id], unit, range: {low, high}, not_to_failure}) from record.rep_range (whiteboard rep_range reports source override:<id>).
Never add custom ids to rules.heavy_squats / heavy_hinges or staples: heavy spine sets and fix staples stay library-only.
Pass customs to the ranker as state.custom (rank.py already supports it); suggestion pools skip custom: true.

reads_audit.check_program.py: muscles, type (rest minutes), patterns (pattern_gap slots), legacy PAT map (push / pull, redundant_pattern), HEAVY id lists (spine sets), stretch_biased id lists
reads_audit.analysis.py: muscles, fatigue, type, swap.flags (unilateral), swap.stretch_emphasis, swap.systemic_fatigue, movement_pattern via movement.py, stretch_biased id lists
reads_audit.suggest.py: muscles, fatigue, type, name, custom (excluded from candidates)
reads_audit.swap.py: muscles, equipment, fatigue, type, name, pattern / PAT, patterns, untracked_target, stretch lists
reads_audit.rank.py: muscles, heads, type, equipment, equipment_needs, patterns, swap ordinals + flags (spinal_load, systemic_fatigue), custom; state.custom pool
reads_audit.whiteboard.py: muscles (primary_region via rules.body_regions), swap.flags (unilateral -> per side), rep_ranges overrides by id, short_name
reads_audit.warmup.py / prs.py / exercise_dsl.py: equipment, bodyweight_fraction, bodyweight_assisted, type, muscles (prs.py already merges history.customExercises)
reads_audit.check_priority.py / muscle_deepdive.py: muscles, name, fatigue, type (through analysis / check_program); deep-dive ranked_adds skips custom
reads_audit.templates.py: movement_pattern, patterns, type, name (preset slots use library ids only)
reads_audit.exercise_detail.py: every field above plus heads, howto, tip (the Builder builds the custom detail popup from the record)

limits: Custom exercises never count as heavy spine sets (spinal_load check) or heavy squat / hinge for the beginner and hinge-before-squat notes: those lists are id-based and stay library-only. The swap flag spinal_load and fatigue 1.5 still feed the ranker and recovery cost.
Stretch credit needs the stretch_focused toggle (it adds the id to rules.stretch_biased[main]); the default comes from the share of library exercises with that pattern and main muscle on the list.

The stretch toggle credits the main mover. 7 library squats / lunges are on the glute stretch list but not the quads list; a custom clone of them with the toggle on would also get quads credit (test: 239 / 246 clones match the library lists exactly, the rest only add the main mover).
exercise_detail.py builds the popup for library ids only; the Builder builds a custom popup from the record (body_map from muscles / heads, fatigue tier, rep range, est. badge).
Templates and presets never use custom ids; fix staples stay library-only, so a fix never suggests a custom exercise.

round_trip.method: leave-one-out over the library (defaults recomputed without the exercise); the form uses the exercise's real bands (main = its top muscle, helper >= 0.4, minor >= 0.25), unilateral flag and stretch-list membership

muscles.note: error from snapping real ratings to 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.3 (counted ratings only)
